college.name: Orange Coast College
college.why: Highest summer CCAP cap (10 units) in OC, deepest online catalog, accepts statewide enrollment for only $42 one-time fee.
college.region_label: Orange County (Anaheim, Huntington Beach, Costa Mesa, Newport Beach)

sequence.reason: Cal-GETC Area 2. Required for nursing and health programs
Cal-GETC Area 4. Highly relevant to health fields

target.label: UC (University of California)
target.note: Complete the full Cal-GETC (7 areas) for maximum impact. Important: UC grants elective and lower-division credit for dual enrollment units, but a minimum residency requirement (36 upper-division units at the UC) means the fastest realistic graduation is still 2 years. Units reduce lower-division course load significantly. Freeing time for upper-division major coursework from day one.

grade_roadmap.summer_action: Apply to summer program at your target college now. One course (3 units) is ideal for a first attempt. English 1A is the top priority.
grade_roadmap.school_year_action: Confirm whether your high school has a CCAP partnership (ask your counselor). If yes, enroll in one dual enrollment course in spring semester.
grade_roadmap.milestone: By end of 9th grade: 3–6 transferable units banked.
grade_roadmap.warning: Some colleges require students to be in 10th grade or older. Check eligibility at your specific college before applying.

grade_roadmap.summer_action: Take 2 courses in summer (6 units). If English 1A is done, move to a Cal-GETC Area 2 or Area 4 course next.
grade_roadmap.school_year_action: Enroll in 1–2 dual enrollment courses during the school year via CCAP. Balance with sophomore-year coursework.
grade_roadmap.milestone: By end of 10th grade: 6–15 transferable units banked.
grade_roadmap.warning: Don't take non-transferable courses. Verify every course is on ASSIST.org (assist.org) before enrolling.

grade_roadmap.summer_action: This is the high-output summer. Max out the summer unit cap at your target college. Two courses minimum.
grade_roadmap.school_year_action: 2 dual enrollment courses + AP strategy. Don't double-count. If you're taking AP Psych, skip Psych 1 at the CCC. Use AP for overlapping subjects, CCC for subjects without an AP option.
grade_roadmap.milestone: By end of 11th grade: 18–35 transferable units. Cal-GETC should be 50–75% complete.
grade_roadmap.warning: Watch the unit caps. Exceeding them can cause enrollment issues. Confirm limits with both your high school and the community college each semester.

grade_roadmap.summer_action: Summer before senior year: cement any remaining Cal-GETC gaps. By this summer you should have 25+ units already.
grade_roadmap.school_year_action: Max out dual enrollment during senior year. If ADT is within reach, pursue it. The CSU admission guarantee is worth it. Request official transcripts from all CCCs attended by April.
grade_roadmap.milestone: By high school graduation: 30–60 transferable units. Cal-GETC complete. ADT filed (if CSU-bound).
grade_roadmap.warning: Apply for ADT by the deadline. It's not automatic. File with the Admissions office at your community college and have transcripts sent to CSU by the application deadline.

cal_getc_areas.example: Art History, Music, Film, or Theater

common_mistakes.title: Taking non-transferable courses
common_mistakes.detail: Every course must appear on ASSIST.org as transferable to UC or CSU before you enroll. Remedial math, ESL courses, and some vocational courses don't count. Verify first, always.

common_mistakes.title: Missing enrollment deadlines
common_mistakes.detail: Summer programs fill fast. Many close in March or April for June sessions. Set a calendar reminder each January to apply for the following summer.

common_mistakes.title: Exceeding unit caps without checking
common_mistakes.detail: Enrolling in more units than your CCAP or concurrent enrollment agreement allows can result in dropped enrollment or loss of fee waiver. Confirm your cap with both your high school counselor and the community college each semester.

common_mistakes.title: Letting AP and dual enrollment overlap
common_mistakes.detail: If you're taking AP Psychology, don't also take Psych 1 at a CCC. You can't use both for the same Cal-GETC area. Use AP for subjects where you have the strongest shot at a 4 or 5; use CCC for subjects with no AP option.

common_mistakes.title: Forgetting to request official transcripts
common_mistakes.detail: Units only transfer if the receiving college gets an official transcript from the CCC. Request transcripts from every community college attended before submitting your college application. This step trips up more families than almost anything else.
